key_insight: Chen et al. show that an AI system can act like an autonomous X-ray scientist, using a large language model to align single crystals at a real synchrotron beamline. This demonstrates that LLM-driven agents can support adaptive, closed-loop experimentation in complex scientific environments.
problem_solved: Traditional synchrotron experiments require expert human intervention to align samples and adjust procedures in real time, which is slow and labor-intensive. This paper addresses the challenge of automating that high-precision, decision-heavy workflow at large-scale scientific facilities.
method: Built an agentic AI workflow that uses an LLM to plan and execute experimental actions.
Integrated the system with a real synchrotron beamline to autonomously align single-crystal samples.
Enabled closed-loop operation, where the AI observes outcomes and adapts its next steps in real time.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this is a concrete example of agentic AI moving beyond text tasks into real-world scientific control. It highlights how LLMs can be combined with tools, sensors, and feedback loops to automate expert-level experimental work.
visual_elements: Workflow diagram showing LLM -> beamline control -> measurement feedback -> next action
Illustration of a synchrotron beamline with a crystal sample being aligned
Closed-loop feedback loop icon or cycle graphic
Before/after comparison of manual vs autonomous crystal alignment
paper_title: An agentic artificially intelligent X-ray scientist
paper_authors: Zhantao Chen, Alexander N. Petsch, Aidan J. Israelski, Rajan Plumley, Lingjia Shen
